note: Rerun with web access. PubMed, ahajournals, diabetesjournals and professional.heart.org returned 403/cookie walls to WebFetch and curl; Europe PMC and other pages used instead. Claims with no opened supporting page are marked unverifiable.

questions.note: Correct for 2017; the 2025 AHA/ACC guideline supersedes it and keeps the 130/80 threshold.
Consistent with GINA 2025 (SABA-only not recommended; ICS-formoterol Track 1 preferred).
Answer unaffected, but the 2024 ADA/EASD/JBDS/AACE/DTS hyperglycemic-crises consensus delays insulin until K >3.5 mmol/L (lesson says 3.3).
Norepinephrine remains first-line in Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2026.

claims.claim: ACC/AHA favor primary PCI with a ~90-minute goal and fibrinolysis if PCI cannot be reached within ~120 minutes of first contact.
claims.note: Current guideline is the 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI ACS guideline: FMC-to-device <=90 min (1A); fibrinolysis when anticipated PPCI delay >120 min from FMC (1A). Lesson names no year; consider citing 2025.

claims.claim: Everyone gets aspirin early; secondary prevention includes high-intensity statin, antiplatelet therapy, beta-blocker and cardiac rehabilitation.
claims.note: 2025 ACS guideline: aspirin load 1A, early oral beta-blocker 1A, high-intensity statin 1A, DAPT >=12 months, cardiac rehab referral.

claims.claim: Fibrinolysis ideally within 30 minutes of arrival at a non-PCI center; morphine no longer routine.
claims.note: Opened summaries did not quote the 30-minute door-to-needle target or the morphine wording; search snippets indicate FMC-to-needle <=30 min and opioids only for refractory pain.

claims.claim: The 2022 ACC/AHA/HFSA guideline: HFrEF is EF <=40%, HFpEF >=50%, four foundational classes (ARNi/ACEi/ARB, beta-blocker, MRA, SGLT2i).
claims.note: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA guideline remains the current comprehensive US HF guideline as of Oct 2026 (an update is listed as in progress).

claims.claim: SGLT2 inhibitors reduce HF hospitalization in HFpEF.
claims.note: 2022 guideline gives SGLT2i a 2a recommendation in HFmrEF/HFpEF.

claims.claim: ACE inhibitor to sacubitril-valsartan requires a 36-hour washout; ICD for EF <=35% after >=3 months of therapy.
claims.note: Not confirmed on an opened page (AHA/PubMed pages blocked); consistent with labeling knowledge only.

claims.claim: The ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS guideline of 2023 increased emphasis on early rhythm control and risk-factor modification.
Anticoagulation is generally recommended at CHA2DS2-VASc >=2 in men and >=3 in women.
claims.note: 2023 guideline frames the threshold as annual stroke risk >=2%, equivalent to these scores. (ESC 2024 uses CHA2DS2-VA without sex.)

claims.claim: DOACs are preferred over warfarin except in moderate-severe mitral stenosis or a mechanical valve.
The 2017 ACC/AHA guideline defines hypertension as >=130/80 mmHg (presented as the current US reference).
claims.note: Out of date: the 2025 AHA/ACC high blood pressure guideline (Aug 2025) supersedes 2017. It keeps 130/80 (stage 1 130-139/80-89) and a <130/80 goal for all adults, and the same first-line classes. Update the citation.

claims.claim: Endocarditis echocardiography is interpreted with the modified Duke criteria; at least three blood-culture sets from separate sites.
claims.note: Out of date: the 2023 Duke-ISCVID criteria update the 2000 modified Duke criteria (adds PET/CT, cardiac CT, PCR/sequencing, intraoperative inspection; removes timing/separate-venipuncture requirements for cultures). Three sets before antibiotics is still sound practice.

claims.claim: Dental prophylaxis is reserved for prosthetic valves, prior endocarditis, certain congenital heart disease and cardiac transplant valvulopathy (AHA 2007 onward).
claims.note: 2021 AHA scientific statement made no changes to the 2007 recommendations.

claims.claim: GINA (report of 2024) recommends that even mild asthma not be treated with SABA alone; ICS-formoterol as-needed is a preferred approach.
claims.note: Version out of date, substance correct: GINA 2025 keeps SABA-only not recommended and ICS-formoterol (Track 1) preferred; a GINA 2026 strategy report is posted on ginasthma.org (May 2026). Cite the current year.

claims.claim: GOLD (report of 2024): long-acting bronchodilator base therapy; ICS added for continued exacerbations with eosinophils >=300/uL.
claims.note: Version out of date, substance largely correct: GOLD 2026 (published Dec 1, 2025) is current; LABA+LAMA base, ICS considered with eos >=300, and GOLD 2026 now advises escalation after even one moderate exacerbation.

claims.claim: Long-term oxygen prolongs survival when resting PaO2 <=55 mmHg or saturation <=88%.
claims.note: Standard GOLD criterion but no reliable primary page was opened (GOLD PDF too large).

claims.claim: The ESC guideline of 2019 defines high-risk PE by hemodynamic instability and calls for systemic thrombolysis, with catheter-directed or surgical embolectomy as alternatives.
claims.note: Accurate for ESC 2019, but a US guideline now exists: 2026 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ACEP/CHEST et al. acute PE guideline (July 2026) with new clinical categories A-E and broader roles for catheter-directed therapy. Lesson should mention it.

claims.claim: ATS/IDSA 2019: outpatients without comorbidity get amoxicillin, doxycycline or a macrolide (if local resistance low); ward inpatients get beta-lactam plus macrolide or a respiratory fluoroquinolone.
claims.note: Macrolide only where pneumococcal macrolide resistance <25%. Search results indicate a 2025 ATS update on selected questions (e.g., withholding antibiotics in virus-positive healthy outpatients); not opened.

claims.claim: Empyema/complicated parapneumonic effusion is drained when pleural pH is below 7.2 or pus is present.
Restrictive transfusion threshold about 7 g/dL and endoscopy within 24 hours for upper GI bleeding.
claims.note: ACG 2021 UGIB guideline. Note: ACG reached no consensus on pre-endoscopic PPI, which the lesson presents as routine.

claims.claim: UC treatment steps from aminosalicylates to biologics such as anti-TNF, vedolizumab and ustekinumab; toxic megacolon needs surgical consultation.
claims.note: 2025 ACG UC guideline update also lists IL-23 inhibitors and JAK inhibitors.

claims.claim: Colonoscopic surveillance for dysplasia begins after about eight years of colitis.
claims.note: Search snippet from ACG 2019 UC guideline states 8 years, but the opened 2025 summary did not state it.

claims.claim: Hepatitis C screening is recommended once for all adults by the USPSTF of 2020.
claims.note: USPSTF (March 2, 2020, grade B) covers adults aged 18 to 79, not all adults; periodic rescreening for ongoing risk. (CDC 2020 says all adults >=18.)

claims.claim: SBP is diagnosed by ascitic neutrophil count >=250/uL and treated with a third-generation cephalosporin plus albumin; paracentesis for anyone admitted with ascites.
claims.note: PMN >=250 cells/mm3; third-generation cephalosporins first line; all with cirrhosis and ascites admitted should have diagnostic paracentesis. Albumin not confirmed in extracted text.

claims.claim: Acute pancreatitis: 2 of 3 criteria (pain, lipase/amylase >3x ULN, imaging); goal-directed fluids, early oral feeding, antibiotics only for infection, ERCP only with cholangitis/obstruction, same-admission cholecystectomy for mild gallstone pancreatitis.
claims.note: 2024 ACG acute pancreatitis guideline; LR preferred, moderate (not aggressive) fluids.

claims.claim: KDIGO AKI: creatinine rise of 0.3 mg/dL within 48 hours or 1.5-fold from baseline within a week.
claims.note: Also urine output <0.5 mL/kg/h for 6 h.

claims.claim: KDIGO 2024: ACEi/ARB with albuminuria, SGLT2i in diabetic and many nondiabetic CKD with adequate eGFR, finerenone in diabetic kidney disease with albuminuria; CKD defined by abnormalities >3 months.
claims.note: SGLT2i threshold eGFR >=20.

claims.claim: Prerenal azotemia: FENa below 1 percent, BUN:Cr >20; ATN: FENa above 2 percent with muddy brown casts.
claims.note: Textbook values; no page opened.

claims.claim: Chronic hyponatremia must not be corrected more than 8 mEq/L in 24 hours in high-risk patients to avoid osmotic demyelination.
claims.note: Search snippets cite the US/Irish expert panel (<=8 mmol/L per 24 h in high-risk; 10-12 average risk), but the CJASN page returned 402 and was not read.

claims.claim: Anion gap normal near 8 to 12; MUDPILES causes of high-gap acidosis.
claims.note: Not checked against an opened page; normal range is assay-dependent.

claims.claim: Hyperkalemia emergency: IV calcium first, then insulin-glucose and beta agonists, then removal.
claims.note: Not checked against an opened page.

claims.claim: DKA: give IV insulin only after confirming potassium is at least about 3.3 mEq/L.
claims.note: 2024 ADA/EASD/JBDS/AACE/DTS hyperglycemic-crises consensus (June 2024): if K <3.5 mmol/L, replace at ~10 mmol/h and postpone insulin until K >3.5. The 3.3 threshold is from the 2009 ADA statement.

claims.claim: HHS: glucose often above 600 mg/dL with effective osmolality above about 320.
claims.note: 2024 consensus HHS criteria: glucose >=600 mg/dL AND calculated effective osmolality >300 mOsm/kg or total osmolality >320; BHB <3.0 mmol/L. DKA now: glucose >=200 or known diabetes, BHB >=3.0 mmol/L, pH <7.3 or HCO3 <18. Lesson does not give the updated DKA criteria.

claims.claim: The ADA Standards of Care of 2024 (updated annually) keep metformin as a common first drug; GLP-1 RA or SGLT2i favored in ASCVD, HF or CKD independent of A1c.
claims.note: Dated: the current edition is Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026, which recommends considering GLP-1 RA/SGLT2i from diagnosis as disease-modifying therapy and moves away from 'lifestyle plus metformin first'. The cardiorenal-indication part is still correct.

claims.claim: Propylthiouracil is preferred in the first trimester of pregnancy.
claims.note: ATA: PTU preferred until week 16.

claims.claim: An adrenal incidentaloma should always prompt checking metanephrines, an aldosterone-to-renin ratio if hypertensive, and a dexamethasone suppression test.
claims.note: 2023 ESE/ENSAT guideline: metanephrines are NOT needed when the mass is <=10 HU on unenhanced CT; DST may be omitted in frail patients with limited life expectancy. ARR with hypertension or unexplained hypokalemia is correct.

claims.claim: Thionamide agranulocytosis: a patient with fever and sore throat should be tested at once.
claims.note: ATA 2016 guidance (stop drug, urgent CBC) seen only in search snippet.

claims.claim: Thalassemia trait shows a Mentzer index below 13.
claims.note: Tertiary source; screening heuristic only.

claims.claim: Only B12 deficiency (not folate) raises methylmalonic acid and causes subacute combined degeneration.
claims.note: Not checked against an opened page.

claims.claim: Iron deficiency in an adult man or postmenopausal woman demands GI evaluation including colonoscopy and endoscopy.
claims.note: Consistent with AGA 2020 iron-deficiency guideline per knowledge; no page opened.

claims.claim: Apixaban and rivaroxaban are reversed with andexanet alfa or prothrombin complex concentrate.
claims.note: Out of date for the U.S.: andexanet alfa (Andexxa) was withdrawn from the US market on Dec 22, 2025 after ANNEXA-I showed doubled thrombosis (14.6% vs 6.9%). In the US, PCC is the remaining option for factor Xa inhibitor reversal; still conditionally authorized in EU/UK.

claims.claim: HIT: score with 4Ts, stop all heparin, start a nonheparin anticoagulant such as argatroban or fondaparinux; do not start warfarin until platelets recover.
claims.note: ASH 2018 HIT guideline; DOACs are also listed options.

claims.claim: TTP is caused by ADAMTS13 deficiency and needs urgent plasma exchange.
claims.note: ISTH 2020 (endorsed by ERBP): TPE plus steroids immediately; rituximab and caplacizumab may be added. A 2025 ISTH focused update exists (not opened).

claims.claim: USPSTF: colorectal screening 45-75 (2021); breast biennial 40-74 (2024); lung LDCT 50-80, >=20 pack-years, quit within 15 years (2021).
claims.note: CRC May 18, 2021; breast April 30, 2024; lung March 9, 2021.

claims.claim: Cervical cancer: cytology every 3 years 21-29, then cytology, hrHPV or both up to 65 (USPSTF 2018).
claims.note: Still the final rec; a Dec 10, 2024 USPSTF draft prefers primary hrHPV every 5 years at 30-65, including patient self-collection. PSA (2018) page notes an update in progress.

claims.claim: PSA screening is an individual decision for men 55-69 (2018); one-time AAA ultrasound for men 65-75 who ever smoked.
claims.note: PSA May 8, 2018 (grade C), update in progress; AAA Dec 10, 2019 (grade B).

claims.claim: Febrile neutropenia is temperature >=38.3 C with ANC below about 500/uL and needs antipseudomonal beta-lactam within an hour.
claims.note: IDSA: single oral temp >=38.3 C or >=38.0 C sustained 1 h; antibiotics within 1 h; cefepime, pip-tazo or carbapenem. StatPearls defines neutropenia as ANC <1500 with severe <500; IDSA FN uses <500 or expected to fall below 500.

claims.claim: Rasburicase is avoided in G6PD deficiency; tumor lysis gives hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, hypocalcemia, hyperuricemia.
claims.note: Not checked against an opened page.

claims.claim: CML has t(9;22) producing BCR-ABL; APL has t(15;17) PML-RARA treated at first suspicion with ATRA.
claims.note: Not checked against an opened page.

claims.claim: The Surviving Sepsis Campaign guideline of 2021: antimicrobials within 1 hour in shock/probable sepsis, ~30 mL/kg balanced crystalloid, norepinephrine first-line, MAP 65.
claims.note: Version out of date, substance unchanged: SSC 2026 guidelines were published March 23, 2026 and keep antimicrobials ideally within 1 h, cultures before antibiotics, >=30 mL/kg crystalloid (conditional), balanced crystalloids, norepinephrine first-line, MAP 65.

claims.claim: Adult empiric meningitis therapy is vancomycin plus ceftriaxone with ampicillin over age 50 or immunocompromised; dexamethasone with or before the first dose; cultures and antibiotics before CT when imaging delays LP.
claims.note: IDSA 2004 guideline (still the IDSA community-acquired meningitis guideline).

claims.claim: IDSA/SHEA 2021 focused update prefers fidaxomicin over oral vancomycin for an initial C. difficile episode; fulminant disease gets high-dose oral vancomycin plus IV metronidazole.
claims.note: Fidaxomicin preference is conditional and resource-dependent; not used in fulminant CDI.

claims.claim: PCP prophylaxis with TMP-SMX at CD4 <200, covering Toxoplasma (CD4 <100); MAC prophylaxis not routine when ART started promptly.
claims.note: Toxoplasma prophylaxis only if Toxoplasma IgG positive.

claims.claim: CDC 2021 STI guidelines: ceftriaxone for gonorrhea, doxycycline for chlamydia; benzathine penicillin G for primary syphilis and in pregnancy.
claims.note: Gonorrhea ceftriaxone 500 mg IM (1 g if >=150 kg).

claims.claim: DHHS recommends ART for everyone with HIV as soon as possible, built around an INSTI plus two NRTIs.
claims.note: clinicalinfo.hiv.gov returned 403. Search snippets indicate current DHHS guidance favors second-generation INSTI plus one or two NRTIs (e.g., DTG/3TC), so 'plus two NRTIs' is incomplete.

claims.claim: ACR 2020 gout: allopurinol first-line ULT for frequent flares or tophi, with flare prophylaxis during initiation.
claims.note: Released May 11, 2020; prophylaxis 3-6 months; treat-to-target urate <6 mg/dL.

claims.claim: In GCA high-dose glucocorticoids are started before the temporal artery biopsy.
claims.note: 2021 ACR/VF guideline: biopsy within 2 weeks of starting glucocorticoids; IV pulse conditionally for threatened vision loss.

claims.claim: Urate crystals are needle-shaped and negatively birefringent; CPPD rhomboid and positively birefringent.
claims.note: Not checked against an opened page.

claims.claim: AGS Beers Criteria updated in 2023 list first-generation antihistamines, benzodiazepines and long-acting sulfonylureas such as glyburide.
claims.note: 2023 update extends the avoid-sulfonylurea advice to all sulfonylureas (incl. short-acting glipizide), not only long-acting ones.

claims.claim: USPSTF 2025 recommends osteoporosis screening in women 65+ and younger postmenopausal women at increased risk; osteoporosis is T-score <= -2.5.
claims.note: Final Jan 14, 2025, grade B; men grade I.

claims.claim: Anti-amyloid antibodies are newer Alzheimer therapies with modest effects and risk of ARIA.
claims.note: Lecanemab (2023) and donanemab (July 2, 2024) are FDA-approved; aducanumab also received accelerated approval in 2021.
